skill.name: openserv-launch
skill.description: Use the OpenServ Launch API to create ERC-20 tokens on Base with Aerodrome concentrated liquidity, locked LP positions, and token lookup workflows.
skill.summary: Launch and inspect Base ERC-20 tokens through the OpenServ Launch API.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: Most high-risk static alerts are false positives from TypeScript template literals, Markdown code fences, and token locker terminology. The real risks are intentional external OpenServ API calls, public Base Mainnet launch side effects, and unpinned remote update commands. No evidence of prompt injection, ransomware behavior, filesystem abuse, or secret exfiltration was found.

remediation.issue: Token launches can occur through the agent example without a shown final approval gate.
remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit confirmation step before POST /api/launch, showing token metadata, wallet, endpoint, and Base Mainnet consequences.

remediation.issue: The skill relies on external OpenServ API calls for launch and token lookup workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Document every outbound endpoint and require users to verify the destination before sending launch metadata.

remediation.issue: The update section uses unpinned npx commands that can change installed skills.
remediation.suggestion: Pin tool versions or link to verified installation guidance with integrity expectations.

remediation.issue: Example files reference environment variables for wallet and API key configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Keep env.example as placeholders only and warn users not to commit real .env files.

static_findings.snippet: systemPrompt: `You are a token launch assistant. You help users create new ERC-20 tokens on Base blo
*   - A valid Ethereum wallet address to receive fees
console.log('\n💡 Tip: Make sure CREATOR_WALLET is a valid Ethereum address')
| 400    | Validation error (invalid name, symbol, wallet, etc.) |
- `reference.md` - Full API reference for all endpoints
| `/api/launch`         | POST   | Create a new token with LP pool  |
| `/api/tokens/:address`| GET    | Get token details by address     |
| `symbol`    | string | Yes      | Token symbol (1-10 chars, uppercase, alphanumeric) |
| `wallet`    | string | Yes      | Creator wallet address (receives 50% of fees)   |
| `imageUrl`  | string | No       | Direct link to image file (jpg, png, gif, webp, svg) |
| `website`   | string | No       | Website URL (must start with http/https)        |
| `twitter`   | string | No       | Twitter handle (with or without @)              |
- Verify the JSON is valid (no trailing commas, properly quoted strings)
**Problem:** The `wallet` field is not a valid Ethereum address.
- Ensure all characters are valid hexadecimal (0-9, a-f, A-F)
- Use a different creator wallet address

content.value_statement: Launching a Base token requires API fields, wallet details, and launch checks. This skill provides OpenServ API guidance, examples, and troubleshooting for token launches.
actual_capabilities: Explains the OpenServ POST launch request fields for creating ERC-20 tokens on Base.
Shows TypeScript examples that call the launch, list, and token detail endpoints.
Documents Aerodrome pool, locker, transaction hash, and explorer link response fields.
Provides an OpenServ agent example with a token launch capability.
Troubleshoots validation errors, rate limits, wallet checks, and transaction failures.
limitations: It depends on the external OpenServ Launch API and Base Mainnet availability.
It does not manage private keys or sign transactions directly.
Token launches are public blockchain actions with lasting consequences.
API behavior may change after the bundled documentation is published.

use_cases.title: Integrate Token Launches
use_cases.description: Build a service that submits token metadata and a creator wallet to the OpenServ launch endpoint.

use_cases.title: Add Agent Launch Capability
use_cases.description: Create an OpenServ agent that collects launch fields and calls the launch API after user approval.

use_cases.title: Debug Launch Failures
use_cases.description: Map API validation, rate limit, and transaction errors to clear recovery steps.

prompt_templates.prompt: Help me prepare the required token name, symbol, wallet, and optional metadata for an OpenServ launch.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Integration Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my plan for calling the OpenServ launch and token listing endpoints from a TypeScript service.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Guarded Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an OpenServ agent capability that launches tokens only after explicit human confirmation and clear risk disclosure.

output_examples.input: What happens when I launch a token?
output_examples.output: The API creates a Base ERC-20 token, an Aerodrome pool, a locked LP position, and public trading links.

output_examples.input: Check my launch plan before I submit it.
output: Confirm the creator wallet is a valid Base mainnet address.
Verify the token name, symbol, image URL, website, and Twitter handle.
Confirm that the launch is intended before calling the API.

output_examples.input: The API says the daily launch limit was reached.
output_examples.output: Wait 24 hours from the prior launch or use a different eligible creator wallet.

best_practices: Require explicit user confirmation before any launch request is sent.
Verify wallet addresses, token metadata, and public links before launch.
Keep API keys and local environment files out of source control.
anti_patterns: Launching tokens from an autonomous agent without a final human approval step.
Using placeholder wallets, image URLs, or websites in production launch requests.
Running update or install commands from untrusted repositories without review.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps you use the OpenServ Launch API to launch and inspect Base ERC-20 tokens.

faq.question: Does the skill deploy tokens by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions and examples that call the external OpenServ API.

faq.question: Which blockchain network does it target?
faq.answer: The documentation targets Base Mainnet, using Aerodrome concentrated liquidity pools.

faq.question: Does it require private keys?
faq.answer: The examples do not handle private keys. They use wallet addresses and external API calls.

faq.question: What data is sent to OpenServ?
faq.answer: Launch requests can send token metadata, creator wallet addresses, websites, image URLs, and Twitter handles.

faq.question: Is it safe for autonomous agents?
faq.answer: Use it with a human confirmation gate because launches are public Base Mainnet actions.
